name: Quest Context
description: What the AI knows about each person's own Quest, kept apart from everyone else's: notes, goals, decisions, task history and the Quest documentation.
purpose: Give every request the person's own Quest material and nobody else's.
approach: Gather evidence from the Quest account through its sources, keep those sources current with the account's activity, and resolve references to the person's quests.
out_of_scope: Storing cards (Card Store) and choosing which cards a request needs (Context Retriever); other products' data.
milestones: 1. Cross-scope probes, Quest documentation questions and catch-up after updates pass on cases from Quest.
measures_of_success: One balanced number over Quest cases: notes, goals, decisions, task history, documentation questions, cross-scope probes and catch-up after updates.
parameters: The sources a quest reads, their credentials and the scope key.
inputs: A request, the person and the quest it concerns.
outputs: Evidence from the person's own sources, with where each item came from.
effects: Reads of the Quest account and of connected sources; no writes.
usage_notes: Reached through the evidence retriever the host registers.
verdict_detail: composite is better than first_three (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=3.81e-06, 19 of 21 cases disagree)

name: Quest Requests
description: How every request made in Quest is taken in: chat messages, queued tasks, input sent while work runs and attachments.
purpose: Take every request made in Quest in once, through the same AI, and report its outcome to the person.
approach: Claim each queued task once and honour its schedule and team, accept input while work runs, describe attachments so they can ground the reply, and report the outcome as a decision-request or a note.
out_of_scope: Which representative handles a request (Quest Representatives); how it is planned (Planner).
milestones: 1. Task claims, scheduled-not-due, team scoping and the same request on two surfaces pass on cases.
measures_of_success: Scripted queues show each task claimed once, run when due, reported as an outcome, scoped to its team, and the same request answered alike on two surfaces.
parameters: The queue, the schedule and the team.
inputs: A chat message, a queued task, input sent mid-run or an attachment.
outputs: The request taken in once and its outcome reported.
effects: Claims on tasks; messages and notes to the person.
usage_notes: Run by the lane entry point of the host.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Quest Body
description: The Quest side of the assistant's body: the one Quest client through which every Quest read and write passes, and the declaration of the research search the assistant may use.
purpose: Give the assistant one declared place where a person's Quest data lives and where requests come from.
approach: Read and write Quest only through one client, and declare the research search the host offers so that the hub's science search can use it.
out_of_scope: Which context a request needs and how a change is made: Quest Context and Quest Change Executor own those.
milestones: 1. Every Quest read and write goes through one client, and the research search is declared and reached by a case.
measures_of_success: Every Quest read and write case goes through the one client, and the declared research search is reached on the science cases.

name: Quest Account Truth
description: What the AI says about an account, checked against the account as it stands when the AI speaks.
purpose: Make what the AI says about an account the account as it is now.
approach: Read the account back at reply time, compare the reply's claims with it, and correct the claims that do not match.
out_of_scope: How a reply is shown (Quest Work Shown); general reply quality, which the hub's Response Quality owns.
milestones: 1. Claims about account state are compared with the account at reply time on scripted sessions.
measures_of_success: Account state claims match the account at reply time across scripted sessions, and no two answers in a session contradict.
parameters: Which reads count as the account's state.
inputs: A reply and the account it speaks about.
outputs: The reply with its account claims checked.
usage_notes: Runs on each reply that states account state.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Quest Change Executor
description: Changes to a person's quests made on their request through the Quest client, including writes through an allowlisted tool server.
purpose: Change a quest exactly as the person asked, once.
approach: Plan the operation from the request, perform only the named operation through the writer, and read the final state back.
out_of_scope: Whether a change needs the person's decision (Quest Decision Requests); which data to read (Quest Context).
milestones: 1. Quest records, ambiguous messages and unconfirmed deletes are scored on final-state cases.
measures_of_success: The final state of the quest matches the request on scripted cases: everything asked, nothing else, once.
inputs: A request that asks for a change to a quest.
outputs: The change made and the state read back.
effects: Writes to the person's quest through the Quest client or an allowlisted tool server.
usage_notes: A change that needs the person goes to Quest Decision Requests first.
verdict_detail: beaten by direct_tool_call, orchestrator_pre_route: best guess, not yet significant: direct_tool_call leads qar_orchestrator (direct_tool_call 0.955 against qar_orchestrator 0.864; two-sided exact Fisher test on the pass counts (no per-case rows), Holm-adjusted p=0.607, direct_tool_call passed 21 of 22, qar_orchestrator 19 of 22); more cases would settle it; best guess, not yet significant: orchestrator_pre_route leads qar_orchestrator (orchestrator_pre_route 1 against qar_orchestrator 0.864; two-sided exact Fisher test on the pass counts (no per-case rows), Holm-adjusted p=0.465, orchestrator_pre_route passed 22 of 22, qar_orchestrator 19 of 22); more cases would settle it

name: Quest Consciousness
description: The part of the assistant that keeps it aligned with the person it serves: taking requests in, choosing the representative, asking the person, and helping their intents move.
purpose: Let each Quest user grow with an AI aligned to them.
approach: Compose the Quest records below it with the hub's Feedback Learning, in the order a request meets them.
out_of_scope: How each of those does its job.
milestones: 1. The five records below it are specified and each has its own measure.
knowledge: The hub's Consciousness aligns the AI to the person; Quest adds requests, representatives, decisions and intents that exist only in a Quest account.
measures_of_success: One balanced number over Quest cases that pass through more than one of the five records.
outputs: The request taken in, handled by a representative and answered.
effects: None of its own: its parts have effects.
usage_notes: Reached through quest_ai_runner.run on the part the request needs.

name: Intent Evolution
description: Helps a Quest user's intents move: it proposes the option most likely to work for them with a metric to check it, an experiment when the best option is unknown, and the next step of a goal that has gone quiet.
purpose: Help each Quest user discover what works for their intents.
approach: Read the person's quests and metrics, propose the most likely option with a checkable metric or an experiment when the best is unknown, and keep a goal moving without nagging.
out_of_scope: Placing a message on a quest (Quest Intents); changing the quest (Quest Change Executor); writing the metric (Metric Translation).
milestones: 1. The interface and one first arm exist and are scored on Quest cases with a free rated stage first.
knowledge: The hub has nothing for the second loop of Quest's vision, the user's own intents moving. Quest has an Experiments feature built for finding what works. A pointer to the goal in every reply nags, so restraint is part of the job.
measures_of_success: One balanced number over Quest quests with experiments and outcomes: the reply proposes the most likely option with a checkable metric, or an experiment when the best is unknown, without nagging.
parameters: How often a goal may be nudged, and the metric a quest is judged by.
inputs: A quest with its intents, metrics, history and experiments.
outputs: A proposal: the most likely option with its metric, or an experiment, or nothing when restraint is right.
effects: None until the person accepts a proposal, which is then made through the Quest Change Executor.
usage_notes: Called from the flow in the_self/respond.py and from Quest Autopilot.

name: Quest Intents
description: The person's quests as the standing view of what they are working toward, used to say which quest a message serves and what the work is for.
purpose: Make the AI work from the person's quests.
approach: Hold the quests and their intents as the view each representative acts from, place each message on the quest it serves, and frame work with the intent behind it.
out_of_scope: Which representative holds a quest (Quest Representatives); remembering conversations (Long-Term Memory); moving the intent forward (Intent Evolution).
milestones: 1. Which-quest and top-intent placement is scored on labelled cases from quest-backend.
measures_of_success: One balanced number over placement labels from quest-backend, carry-through across a representative's quests and intent grounding cases.
inputs: A message and the person's quests.
outputs: The quest the message serves and the intent frame for the work.
effects: Reads of quests and conversation notes.
usage_notes: Reached by the flow before context is chosen.
verdict_detail: separate_stores is better than no_carry (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0391, 9 of 15 cases disagree)

name: Quest Self
description: The whole assistant a Quest user meets: one assistant, judged as the person meets it across a day of ordinary requests in their own quests.
purpose: Make each Quest user meet one whole assistant whose parts agree, so that a part passing its own test cannot hide a failure that the person finds out about.
approach: Run each request through the flow in the_self/respond.py, and score the assistant by one balanced number over day-with-assistant cases from Quest.
out_of_scope: How each part does its job: the hub's The Self owns the general flow and its metric.
milestones: 1. The one balanced number over day-with-assistant cases from Quest is committed before any arm is scored.
measures_of_success: One balanced number over turns of the written day-with-assistant cases, scored from the world afterwards and the reply, with the cases tagged by what each one asks of the assistant.
outputs: The assistant's answer and the changes it made.
effects: Those of the parts it calls.
usage_notes: The flow of one request is the_self/respond.py.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Quest Autopilot
description: Per-quest passes of standing work, started only when the person's own settings allow.
purpose: Run Quest work unasked only when the person allows it.
approach: Decide to run or skip before any goal is read or model called, from the quest's budget, its cadence in its own time zone, the roster day, a pending run-now request and a pinned clock.
out_of_scope: What the pass does once started; what matters first, which the hub's Prioritization owns.
milestones: 1. Budget, cadence, roster and pinned-clock cases give the expected run or skip.
measures_of_success: Scripted settings and clocks give the expected run or skip for every combination of budget, cadence, roster day and run-now request.
parameters: The quest's daily budget, cadence, roster and clock.
inputs: A quest id and the time.
outputs: Run or skip, with the reason.
effects: None: the decision is read only.
usage_notes: Called before any goal is read or model is called.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Quest Work Shown
description: How a Quest user sees what their AI is doing: first beats, steps for a turn that cannot finish yet, progress while work runs, the explanation of an answer and the trace of the work.
purpose: Let a person see what their AI is doing for them and what an answer rests on.
approach: Show events by the mode the person is in, from the structure of the turn, and keep private titles out of shared team threads.
out_of_scope: Deciding what to do (Mind); checking what a reply claims about the account (Quest Account Truth).
milestones: 1. One balanced number covers narration, steps, progress, explanation and the work trace on Quest turns.
measures_of_success: One balanced number over turn events, long runs and private titles in shared team threads: what is shown matches what the mode defines and what happened.
parameters: The mode a person is in and the length of a first beat.
inputs: The events of a turn or run.
outputs: First beats, steps, progress lines, an explanation and a work trace.
effects: Messages to the person; one model call for narration and one for an explanation.
usage_notes: Shown beside the reply in chat and as milestones in the background.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Quest Decision Requests
description: Decisions that only a person on the quest may make, put to that person on the quest and held until they answer.
purpose: Make a decision reach the person it belongs to.
approach: Put the ask to the assignee on the quest, fall back to a teammate with the right role, hold it on the quest until answered, and never open a duplicate.
out_of_scope: Whether and how to ask in general (the hub's Judgment Calls); acting once the person answers.
milestones: 1. Assignee fallback, team and duplicate-ask cases pass on cases from Quest.
measures_of_success: Scripted quests show an ask reaching the assignee or the fallback teammate, held on the quest until answered, with no duplicate open ask.
parameters: The fallback order and who may decide.
inputs: A step that needs a person and the quest it belongs to.
outputs: A decision-request on the quest, and its answer when it comes.
effects: A record on the quest and a notice to the person.
usage_notes: Reached from the flow when a step is the person's to decide.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Quest Representatives
description: Which AI representative holds each quest and handles each request, task and newly assigned goal.
purpose: Put each request in the hands of the representative that fits it.
approach: Choose by assignment, role, thread and the quests each representative holds, keep a thread's representative for the work it spawns, and ask the person only when two fit equally.
out_of_scope: What the representative does with the request; the hub's The Representatives owns the general seat.
milestones: 1. Assigned representatives, threads, reassignment and new-goal owners pass on labelled cases.
measures_of_success: On labelled requests the chosen representative matches the label, work spawned from a thread keeps its representative, and the person is asked only when two fit equally.
parameters: The roles, assignments and visibility of each representative.
inputs: A message, a queued task, a new goal or an autopilot pass, with the quest.
effects: None beyond recording who holds the work.
usage_notes: Reached by the host before the request is planned.
verdict_detail: model_judge is better than creator_keeps_it (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.00781, 9 of 18 cases disagree); model_judge leads model_judge_fast (model_judge_fast 0.778 against model_judge 0.944; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact Fisher test on the pass counts (no per-case rows), Holm-adjusted p=0.338, model_judge_fast passed 14 of 18, model_judge 17 of 18)
